findings.title: create_skipped_slot's 0-row re-read maps find_live_row_for_slot DB errors into 409 Conflict, while do_skip maps the same error to 500
findings.evidence:
'Ok(False) ->
  case find_live_row_for_slot(config.db, app_uuid, slot) {
    Ok(Some(row)) if row.status == "skipped" ->
      json_ok(json.object([#("skipped", json.bool(True))]))
    _ ->
      response_helpers.json_error(
        error_code.Conflict,
        "This reference changed state. Refresh and try again.",
        409,
      )
  }' — the `_` arm swallows Error(_). do_skip (line ~394) maps the same helper's Error(_) to a branded 500.
findings.detail: Same Result-returning helper, two call sites, inconsistent handling: a transient DB failure on the re-read is reported to the landlord as a state-change race (409) — a lie about the cause, and inconsistent with the r2 Result-typing fix's own intent.
findings.recommended_fix: Add an explicit `Error(_) -> 500` arm before the `_ -> 409` catch-all in create_skipped_slot's re-read, mirroring do_skip.

findings.title: verify_vacancy_active DB error bypasses the archived-vacancy guard: run_action_with_prechecks' `_ -> action()` catch-all runs the mutation on Error
findings.detail: A transient DB blip on the vacancy read skips the archive guard and runs do_skip/do_re_enable/run_create_checks on an archived vacancy — the exact bypass handle_open was restructured to prevent. Requires a mid-request DB failure, so low likelihood, but the fix is one line.
findings.recommended_fix: Mirror handle_open's three-way split: Error(_) -> branded 500, Ok(_) non-archived -> action(), Ok([]) -> 404, archived -> 422.

findings.title: The 0-row/409 race-guard branches added by the r2 fix have no deterministic test
findings.evidence: Grep of the test file: no test exercises the Ok(False) branch — skip_before_trigger_creates_skipped_row_reserving_slot_test and skip_is_idempotent_test cover the Ok(True)/None arms only; the 0-row conflict needs a live row to appear between read and insert, which no test simulates.
findings.detail: W1's fix — the highest-stakes change in this delta — is guarded by code with no automated pin; a regression that restores the lying 200 skipped:true would pass CI. Concurrency paths are hard to test deterministically, but the decision logic can be extracted.
findings.recommended_fix: Extract the 0-row re-read decision into a pure helper (slot status in → 200/409 out) and unit-test it with a stubbed read result; or add a targeted integration test that pre-inserts a queued row to force the conflict.

findings.title: create_one_slot and create_one_skipped_slot are near-duplicate scaffolds (~35 differing lines: insert query + audit event only)
findings.evidence: Both: 'fn create_one_<x>_slot(tx, app_uuid, landlord_uuid, slot, name, phone, email) -> Result(Bool, String)' -> 'case sql.insert_reference_call_<if_absent|skipped>(...)' -> parse row.id -> audit_log.create with the same details shape -> Ok(True)/Ok(False)/Error. The r2 delta made both return Bool, increasing the shared surface.
findings.detail: AGENTS.md mandates DRY extraction at 2+ repeats. Third consumer of the same scaffold would make this genuinely worth fixing; today it is two copies that must be kept in sync by hand.
findings.recommended_fix: Extract insert_slot_and_audit(tx, insert_fn, audit_event, ...) parameterised on the insert query and audit event. Optional; fine to defer until a third slot-kind appears.

findings.title: find_live_row_for_slot and find_skipped_row_for_slot duplicate the list+filter scaffold, differing only in the status predicate
findings.evidence: Both: 'case sql.list_reference_calls_for_application(db, app_uuid) { Ok(pog.Returned(_, rows)) -> case list.find(rows, fn(row) { row.ref_slot == slot && row.owner_label == primary_owner && <status predicate> }) ... Error(err) -> Error(err) }' — predicates differ only in '!is_terminal(row.status)' vs 'row.status == "skipped"'. The r2 delta re-typed both to Result, making them structurally identical.
findings.detail: Two copies of the same list+filter+Result-shape; the r2 rework touched both identically. A third status query (e.g. the RC3.x sweep) will copy it again.
findings.recommended_fix: Factor find_row_for_slot(db, app, slot, predicate) and pass the predicate per call. Optional; low urgency.

findings.title: Per-handler negative coverage is asymmetric: the r1 changelog claims cross-tenant/archived/unknown-slot coverage for all 3 handlers; handle_skip and handle_re_enable each miss 2 of the 3 negatives
findings.evidence: Handler tests present: handle_start (creates_rows, cross_tenant_is_not_found, archived_vacancy_is_unavailable), handle_skip (unknown_slot_is_bad_request, mid_flight_row_is_conflict), handle_re_enable (round_trips, cross_tenant_is_not_found). Absent: handle_skip cross-tenant 404 + archived 422; handle_re_enable archived 422 + unknown-slot 400. The shared run_action_with_prechecks/is_valid_slot code is exercised via handle_start/handle_skip, so the gap is per-arm wiring only.
findings.detail: The spec Change Log sentence 'HTTP-level coverage of the three handlers (happy 200 + cross-tenant 404 + archived 422 + unknown-slot 400 + mid-flight-skip 409)' reads as per-handler coverage; it is actually the union across handlers. Shared prechecks ARE covered, so impact is low.
findings.recommended_fix: Either add the missing per-handler negatives (4 small tests) or reword the changelog to say the union is covered via the shared precheck functions.
